threads.thread_goal: Align on target account list and pilot scope for the new device program.

messages.text:
Kicking off the new device education and sales program here.

First step is to align on which accounts we target in the pilot and how we tier them.

I have started a draft Target Account Segmentation Sheet for the project_title in A1, linked to task T1. Right now it has our main regions and a first pass at hospitals and larger clinics.

Can everyone review and suggest:
- any missing key accounts
- which ones should be top tier for the first 21-day pilot
- who should own each account

Once we agree, we will lock the pilot scope and number of accounts for wave 1.

Thanks for starting this.

I have gone through A1 and added a few regional clinics that send a lot of referrals for similar devices. I also flagged two teaching hospitals that usually engage well with educational programs.

Question: for the pilot, are we focusing only on hospitals, or do we also want a few high-volume private practices in there?

Good additions, thanks.

On scope: my suggestion is
- Core pilot: top hospitals and teaching centers where we can run webinars and get structured feedback
- Plus: a small number of high-volume private practices per region to test how the program works in smaller settings.

If that sounds reasonable, we can reflect it in the priority tiers in A1.

I have added a few more accounts to A1, but I am not fully sure how to assign the tiers.

Right now I just marked some as important based on recent order history. Can someone double-check the tiering logic before we finalize?

I can help refine the tiers.

For the education-led pilot, maybe we define tiers like this:
- Tier 1: teaching hospitals and large centers where we can run webinars and get multiple clinicians in one session
- Tier 2: regional hospitals with good potential but fewer specialists
- Tier 3: selected private practices with high procedure volume

If you agree, I will add a short description of this logic in A1 so it is clear for everyone.

I have looked at the list in A1 and I think we might be missing a couple of accounts that are very active on social media and usually respond well to digital campaigns.

I will add them under my region and tentatively mark them as Tier 2 unless someone thinks they should be Tier 1.

I like that tiering logic.

I have updated A1 to add a 'Tier definition' tab and applied your Tier 1–3 criteria to the current list. Please check your own accounts and adjust if anything looks off.

Next question: how many accounts do we want in the first pilot wave? Right now, if we take all Tier 1 plus a subset of Tier 2, we are at around 30 accounts.

Given the 21-day window, 30 feels a bit heavy if we want quality interactions and proper logging.

Maybe we cap the first wave at around 15–20 accounts, focusing on Tier 1 and just a few Tier 2 that are very engaged.

From an education and webinar planning perspective, 15–20 accounts is more realistic for the pilot. That would allow us to schedule a few focused sessions and still gather meaningful feedback.

We can always expand to the remaining Tier 2 and Tier 3 accounts after we refine the materials.

I am ok with 15–20 accounts for the first wave.

If we go that route, should we include at least one Tier 3 private practice per region, or keep Tier 3 for later?

My proposal:
- Include all Tier 1 accounts in the pilot
- Add a small number of Tier 2 accounts that are known to be responsive
- Keep Tier 3 for the second wave, unless there is a very strong reason to include a specific practice now.

That should land us around 18 accounts total.

Works for me. I have checked my region and confirmed which Tier 2 accounts I think should be in the first wave.

I also added my name as owner for those accounts in A1.
I have done the same for my region. With the current selection, we are at 17 accounts. If we want to hit 18, I can add one more Tier 2 hospital that has shown interest in similar devices.

Thanks. Please go ahead and add that extra Tier 2 hospital so we land at 18.

Once that is in, I will freeze the 'Pilot wave 1' filter in A1 so we all work from the same list.
From my side, the current pilot list in A1 looks balanced across regions and specialties. It should give us enough variety for the educational sessions without stretching the timeline.

I have now locked the 'Pilot wave 1' view in A1 with 18 accounts selected, all with assigned owners and tiers.

Unless there are strong objections today, I suggest we treat this as our approved pilot list and move on to planning the webinars and sales activities.
No objections from me. The 18-account pilot scope is clear, and the owners are correctly assigned in A1.
All good on my side as well. I will start planning outreach to my pilot accounts once the scripts and materials are ready.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise educational slide deck and sales script.

messages.text:
I have uploaded the first draft of the clinician educational slide deck for the project_title as A2, linked to task T2.

The deck covers indications, mechanism of action, benefits, and safety information, using only approved clinical data. There are placeholders where we still need final wording from regulatory.

Can the sales team review and comment on:
- whether the flow supports your conversations
- any gaps in typical questions you get from clinicians
- anything that might be too technical or not practical for visits?

Thanks for sharing A2.

First impressions:
- The mechanism section is clear, but might be a bit long for a busy clinic visit. Maybe we can move some of the detailed diagrams to an appendix.
- The benefits slide is strong; I would bring that earlier in the deck so we get to the clinical value faster.

I will add comments directly in A2 and suggest a slightly shorter core flow for in-person calls.

I have gone through the deck quickly.

One question: on the safety slide, there are a few terms that I am not sure how to explain simply to clinicians who are not specialists. Could we add a short speaker note with plain-language explanations so we stay accurate but easy to understand?

I like the structure overall.

From recent calls, clinicians often ask about:
- how this device compares to existing options in terms of workflow
- what kind of training is needed for staff

We might want a slide or at least a section in the notes that addresses those points, staying within approved claims.

Great feedback.

I will:
- Move the benefits slide earlier in the deck
- Shift some of the detailed mechanism diagrams to an appendix
- Add speaker notes with simpler explanations on the safety slide, as suggested.

I will update A2 later today and flag the new version in this thread.

I added a couple of comments in A2 where I think we could include more practical examples, like typical patient profiles.

Also, will we have a shorter version of the deck for quick visits, or should we just skip some slides depending on the time?

Good point. For the pilot, I suggest we define:
- a core set of slides for standard visits
- optional appendix slides for deeper dives or webinars.

We can mark these clearly in A2 so everyone knows what to prioritize.

Agreed. I will tag slides as 'Core' or 'Appendix' in A2 and adjust the agenda slide accordingly.

Once that is done, we should be close to a final structure for the deck.

Update: I have now revised A2 with:
- benefits earlier in the flow
- core vs appendix slides clearly marked
- simplified speaker notes on safety
- a short section on workflow and staff training, based on recent questions.

Please take a final look and confirm if this structure works for the pilot.

I have reviewed the updated A2.

The flow feels much more aligned with how we run calls, and the core vs appendix split is clear. From my side, this structure is good to go for the pilot, pending regulatory and medical affairs review.
Same here, the notes on the safety slide help a lot. I am comfortable using this structure in visits once it is approved.

Great, I will now submit A2 for regulatory and medical affairs review as part of T2.

Switching to the sales script: I have also drafted a Standard Sales Script and Objection Guide as A3, linked to T3. It includes:
- opening and needs assessment questions
- key messages aligned with the deck
- top 10 objections with compliant responses.

Please review and flag anything that does not match what you hear in the field.

Looking at A3 now.

The opening questions are good, but I would add one more about current workflow to better position the device.

On objections, I often hear concerns about budget and reimbursement. The guide covers budget, but reimbursement is only briefly mentioned. Can we expand that section, staying within what is approved?
I added a comment in A3 on the closing part. It might help to include a simple summary line we can use to wrap up the call and confirm next steps, like scheduling a demo or webinar.

On the objection guide in A3, I am not fully sure about the wording for the question around off-label use. I want to make sure I do not say anything that could be interpreted as going beyond approved indications.

Could we tighten that answer and maybe add a reminder to stick to the approved claims?

Good catches.

I will:
- add a workflow-focused question to the opening section
- expand the reimbursement objection with approved language
- tighten the off-label response and add a short reminder about staying within approved indications.

Once I update A3, we should send it for regulatory review together with the deck so any requested changes can be captured in T12.

Update: A3 is now revised with the additional workflow question, expanded reimbursement objection, and clarified off-label response.

Please do a final pass so we can lock this for the pilot, subject to regulatory approval.

I have reviewed the latest A3.

The flow from opening to closing feels natural, and the objection responses are clear and aligned with the deck. From my side, this script and guide are ready to use in the pilot once regulatory signs off.
Agreed. The added workflow question and reimbursement detail match what I hear in calls. I am comfortable using this as the standard for the pilot.

Great, I will now submit both A2 and A3 for regulatory and medical affairs review and track any requested edits under T12.

Once we get feedback, we will make final tweaks and confirm the versions for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the digital outreach plan and webinar schedule.

messages.text:
I have drafted a Digital Outreach Plan for the project_title as A4, linked to T4, and a first pass at pilot webinar topics and target accounts for T7.

Proposal:
- Channels: email to HCP lists, LinkedIn posts, and short educational clips we can share after webinars
- Frequency: 1 email per pilot account ahead of the webinar, 1 reminder, and 1 follow-up
- Content themes: clinical need, mechanism and benefits, safety, and case-based tips.

For webinars (T7), I have listed 4 pilot sessions mapped to the 18 accounts in A1.

Please review A4 and the webinar list and share any concerns or additions.

Thanks for putting this together.

On channels: email and LinkedIn make sense. For the pilot, I would avoid adding more channels so we can keep it manageable and compliant.

On webinars: 4 sessions for 18 accounts seems reasonable. We just need to make sure time zones and preferred days are considered for the teaching hospitals.

Looking at A4, I like the idea of short educational clips after webinars.

One question: for LinkedIn, are we posting from our personal profiles, company page, or both? I want to be sure we stay within approved messaging and do not improvise wording.

For my region, early evenings work best for webinars, especially for teaching hospitals.

In the T7 list, two of my accounts are grouped into a midday slot. Could we shift that session later in the day to improve attendance?

I added a comment in A4 suggesting we include a short line in the emails reminding clinicians that the content is educational and based on approved information.

Also, for the follow-up email, can we include a link to A2 or a PDF summary, or should we only send approved materials once regulatory confirms?

On LinkedIn, for the pilot I suggest we:
- use company page posts with pre-approved wording
- allow personal profiles to share those posts without changing the text.

I will reflect this in A4 and make sure the sample posts are written in a way that is easy to share without edits.

Good point on timing.

I will adjust the T7 schedule so that your region's session is in the early evening. We will also add a note in A4 that webinar times should be adapted to local preferences where possible.

On follow-up content: we should only link to A2 or any PDF once regulatory and medical affairs have approved the final versions.

For now, in A4 we can specify that follow-up emails will include either the approved deck or a short approved summary, depending on what regulatory signs off.

I have now updated A4 with:
- clarified LinkedIn approach (company posts shared by reps)
- compliance reminder line in emails
- note that follow-up content depends on approved materials
- reference to time-zone adjustments.

For T7, I have:
- 4 webinars scheduled over two weeks
- each mapped to specific pilot accounts from A1
- tentative presenters listed (myself plus one rep per session).

Please confirm if the channels and content types in A4, and the 4-webinar plan in T7, work for the pilot.

From my side, the channel mix (email plus LinkedIn) and the content types in A4 are appropriate for the pilot. The 4-webinar schedule in T7 also looks balanced across the 18 accounts.

I am comfortable locking this plan for the pilot.
Confirmed for my accounts: the assigned webinar slots and email cadence work. I will start lining up key contacts once the invitations are approved.
All good for my region as well. The company-page LinkedIn approach makes it easier to stay on message.
No further comments from me. I will prepare my pilot accounts for the webinar invites and follow the email plan in A4.

threads.thread_goal: Align on CRM logging, KPIs and reporting expectations.

messages.text:
I have created a KPI Tracking Dashboard Template as A6, linked to T6, and a draft CRM logging guideline as A8, aligned with T10 and the pre-call checklist A5.

A6 includes fields for account, stage (lead, demo, order), estimated value, and next step. The first tab defines each KPI.

A8 outlines which CRM fields to use for the new device and how to log webinars, calls, and follow-ups.

Please review and let me know if anything is unclear or missing for your day-to-day use.

Thanks for setting this up.

Looking at A6, the main KPIs for the pilot seem to be:
- number of leads per account
- number of demos or webinar attendees
- number of orders and their value.

I would also like to track a simple engagement score, maybe by counting meaningful interactions per account (questions asked, follow-up requests). We could capture that in a notes field or a simple rating.

In A8, the logging process is mostly clear.

One question: for webinar attendees, do we log them as separate contacts under the same account, or just as a single webinar activity linked to the account? I want to avoid double counting in A6.

I have a basic question on A5: before each call, we are supposed to check that we only use approved materials and that we log the interaction in the CRM.

Could we add a quick reminder in A5 about which CRM fields are mandatory for the new device? That would help me avoid missing anything.

In A6, I like the clarity of the stages, but I am not sure when to move an account from lead to demo.

Is it when they attend a webinar, or only when they agree to a dedicated demo session?

Good idea on engagement.

We can add a simple 'Engagement level' column in A6 with a 1–3 scale, defined in the KPI tab, based on the number and quality of interactions.

On webinar logging (M54), my suggestion is:
- log the webinar as one activity per account in the CRM
- list individual attendees in the notes or a separate attendee list, but do not create separate opportunities for each.

I will update A6 and A8 to reflect this.

On stages, I propose we define in A6:
- Lead: account has shown interest or been invited to a webinar
- Demo: account has attended a webinar or a dedicated demo session
- Order: account has placed at least one order for the device.

This keeps it simple and consistent across regions.

Good call.

I will update A5 to include a short section listing the mandatory CRM fields for the new device, aligned with A8. That way, the checklist and the process doc say the same thing.
The engagement level and webinar logging approach make sense to me. It should keep A6 readable while still capturing useful detail.
Thanks for clarifying the stages. With that definition, I know when to move accounts in A6 and in the CRM.

I have now updated A6 with:
- engagement level column and definition
- clear stage definitions (lead, demo, order)

And A8 with:
- webinar logging rules
- alignment with the mandatory fields listed in A5.

Please confirm that this KPI set and the logging process work for the pilot.

I have reviewed the latest A6 and A8.

The KPIs (leads, demos, orders, engagement) and their definitions are clear, and the CRM logging steps are practical for daily use.

From my side, I am ok to adopt this KPI set and logging process for the pilot.
Confirmed. With the added reminders in A5 and the examples in A8, I feel confident about what to log after each interaction.
All good for me as well. I will start using A6 for my pilot accounts and follow the CRM steps in A8.
No further questions. The definitions and examples are clear enough to get started.

threads.thread_goal: Share pilot results, feedback and decide on broader rollout.

messages.text:
We have completed the initial pilot period for the project_title.

I have compiled the KPI data from A6 and the main insights into a draft Post-Pilot Performance and Lessons Report as A7, linked to T11.

Highlights:
- Good engagement from most Tier 1 accounts, mixed from Tier 2
- Webinars drove more demos than individual visits
- A few recurring questions about workflow and reimbursement.

Please review A7 and share your observations from the field so we can decide how to adjust the target account strategy and whether we keep or update the sales script for the broader rollout.

Looking at A6 and A7, a few things stand out:
- Tier 1 teaching hospitals had the highest demo-to-order conversion
- Some Tier 2 accounts with strong digital engagement also performed well
- Tier 2 accounts with low engagement did not move beyond leads.

This suggests we should keep Tier 1 as the core focus and be more selective with Tier 2 in the next phase, prioritizing those with proven engagement.

From my calls (logged under T8), clinicians appreciated the educational focus, but some asked for more concrete workflow examples and short checklists they could share with nursing staff.

On accounts, a couple of Tier 3 practices I know would likely respond well to this kind of program. Maybe we can add a small number of Tier 3 accounts with high potential in the next wave.

I noticed that in some Tier 2 accounts, the webinar invite emails had low open rates, but once we got clinicians into a session, the script from A3 worked well.

Maybe for those accounts we need a different outreach angle or more support from local champions.

On the script in A3, I found that the workflow question and reimbursement objection handling were very useful. I did not feel the need to improvise much.

The only part I sometimes skipped was a longer explanation of the mechanism when time was short. For the broader rollout, maybe we can emphasize that reps can shorten that section if needed.

Thanks for the insights.

On target accounts, based on A6 and A7, I would summarize the options as:
- keep Tier 1 as is
- refine Tier 2 to focus on those with higher engagement scores
- selectively add a few Tier 3 practices with strong potential, as suggested.

If we agree, we can update A1 to reflect this refined strategy for the broader rollout.

I support that approach.

For the next phase, I propose we:
- keep all current Tier 1 accounts
- reclassify low-engagement Tier 2 accounts as lower priority
- add up to 5 Tier 3 practices with clear potential, nominated by reps.

I can coordinate the update to A1 so the new strategy is clearly documented.
Works for me. I already have two Tier 3 practices in mind that match the profile in A7. I will propose them in A1 once we open the next-wave section.
Agreed. I will also review my Tier 2 accounts and flag which ones should stay in the higher-priority group based on engagement in A6.
Great. Once you update A1 with the refined tiers and added Tier 3 practices, we can treat that as our adjusted target account strategy for the broader rollout.

On the sales script in A3, pilot feedback in A7 suggests that:
- the overall structure works
- the workflow and reimbursement sections are particularly valuable
- the mechanism explanation can be shortened in some visits.

Do you think we need to change the script itself for the rollout, or is it enough to add guidance on when to shorten or skip certain parts?

My view: the core script in A3 is solid. I would not change the wording much, to avoid another full review cycle.

Instead, we can add a short usage note at the top of A3 explaining that reps can:
- use the full script for longer visits and webinars
- use a shortened version by focusing on the opening, benefits, workflow, and closing when time is limited.

That should give enough flexibility without altering the approved content.
I agree. A usage note would match how we already adapted the script in practice during the pilot.
Same here. No major changes needed, just clearer guidance on when to go deeper vs keep it short.
I am comfortable keeping the script as is, with the added note. That will help me decide on the fly without worrying about going off track.

Understood. I will add a short usage note to A3 as you described and include that in the final version for rollout.

We will keep the script content itself unchanged, so we do not need a full re-approval, just a quick confirmation that the note is consistent with the approved use.

To wrap up this thread:
- We will refine the target account strategy in A1 based on pilot engagement data from A6 and insights in A7, keeping Tier 1, focusing on engaged Tier 2, and adding a few high-potential Tier 3 practices.
- We will keep the current sales script in A3 for the broader rollout, adding a usage note to guide when to use the full vs shortened version.

I will finalize A7 under T11 with these decisions and share it with stakeholders.
